header.stance: 實質利率與事件風險推升長端殖利率

zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 固定收益開場論點

荷姆茲海峽周邊戰事再起，使上周五的政策重新定價擴大為對存續期間的全面考驗；不過，收盤結構仍不足以確認新一輪通膨衝擊。美國10年期公債殖利率上升2個基點至4.75%，創2025年1月以來新高，30年期殖利率上升3個基點至5.25%。2年期殖利率持平於4.34%，調整集中在前端以外，2s10s擴大2個基點至41個基點，2s30s擴大3個基點至91個基點，殖利率曲線因而陡峭化。美國與伊朗約一個月來首次互相發動攻擊後，WTI期貨上漲3.55%至$86.36。聯準會將如何因應通膨再度成為焦點，能源、期限溢價與供給去化也重回長端定價。

賣壓的細部結構支持較審慎的解讀。10年期實質殖利率上升2個基點至2.44%，升幅與名目殖利率相同，10年期損益兩平通膨率則持平於2.31%。布蘭特期貨也不符合單純的能源通膨敘事；WTI大漲之際，布蘭特反而下跌0.81%至$88.59。投資人提高實質補償要求，並推動曲線陡峭化，卻未在當天調高10年期通膨補償。10年期殖利率全月持平，30年期殖利率仍較月初低2個基點。換言之，周一走勢延續眼前壓力，但既未抹去財政部規劃買回對較長期走勢的支撐，也未證明財政期限溢價再度向上突破。

跨資產交易顯示，壓力集中在存續期間與利率敏感型成長資產，並非融資環境普遍退潮。標普500指數下跌0.58%，那斯達克100指數下跌0.62%，半導體指數下跌2.92%，美元指數則上漲0.26%。投資級信用債總報酬指標受較長存續期間拖累，下跌0.49%；主要高收益債指標僅下滑約0.07%。黃金上漲0.44%，全月漲幅仍達11.09%。市場正受兩股力量拉扯：實質折現率上升壓抑長存續期間資產，但投資人對政策、匯率與地緣政治不確定性的避險需求並未消失。

這個交易日改變的是風險落點；市場仍要求政策以後續行動取信，這項前提沒有改變。上周五的鷹派訊息推高殖利率曲線中對政策敏感的區段；周一油價上漲時，2年期殖利率持平，長端則走高。全周仍呈現先前的熊市趨平，2年期殖利率上升10個基點，10年期與30年期殖利率分別上升5個與2個基點。單日曲線陡峭化說明，即使聯準會的緊縮立場足以取信市場，長債仍無法避開能源中斷、9月大量公司債供給與財政部干預的不確定性。不過，損益兩平通膨率持平，代表這些風險尚未演變成自我強化的通膨判斷。接下來的數據必須釐清，10年期殖利率升至4.75%，究竟反映持久的實質利率壓力，還是市場因事件密集的一周而要求的暫時性溢價。

## 油價重啟長端疑問

這次地緣政治事件已具體到足以左右收盤。美軍攻擊荷姆茲海峽一座島嶼，伊朗則對阿拉伯聯合大公國與約旦發動反擊。美國總統Donald Trump隨後在美國交易時段揚言採取進一步行動。市場重新評估荷姆茲海峽航運恢復正常的可能性，WTI因而升破$86。這不只是又一輪外交警告：約一個月來首次直接交火，使實體供給中斷與運輸成本上升可能一路影響秋季通膨數據。

美國公債走勢仍清楚區分眼前的商品風險與中期通膨預期。5年期殖利率上升1個基點至4.49%，10年期升至4.75%，30年期升至5.25%，2年期則維持在聯準會主席演說後確立的水準。若市場只是提高對9月政策利率的預期，壓力通常會更集中在前端。周一新增的補償反而落在較遠端，因為能源衝擊能持續多久、未來發債規模，以及財政與貨幣政策如何互動，在該區段的定價權重更高。實質殖利率上升也印證這項解讀：即使10年期損益兩平通膨率未動，投資人仍提高對通膨調整後報酬的要求。

月底需求幾乎未能牽制賣壓。紐約時間下午4時指數再平衡前後一分鐘內，12月10年期公債期貨成交近244,000口，接近全日成交量的10%，但長天期美國公債收盤幾乎沒有受益。選擇權需求也轉向防範長債進一步下跌，包括斥資約$650萬買進12月美國長債賣權；相關部位對應11月20日到期時30年期殖利率接近5.7%。這些交易屬於避險，不是預測，但部位落點顯示，前端完成重新定價後，投資人認為最不對稱的風險仍在長端。

財政部擴大買回計畫，是比較各國主權債表現時不能忽略的制約因素。財政部長Scott Bessent指出，美國10年期殖利率8月僅上升約2個基點，相較之下，德國升幅超過10個基點，日本超過15個基點。他為計畫辯護時採取了新的論述：買回旨在減緩市場單向走勢，若未干預，美國公債表現可能更差。Bessent也把原先承諾近期提出的財政整頓簡報，延後到未來數周或數月。前一項說法支撐長端流動性，後一項安排則讓財政錨定不再迫在眉睫；兩者都沒有改變政府必須籌措的資金規模。

實質殖利率上升之際，美元周一僅上漲0.26%，全月仍下跌0.38%。美元反應克制值得注意，因為若政策分歧明確有利美國，匯率通常會獲得更強支撐。投資人一面評估聯準會公信力，一面擔心擴大買回與財政部更積極干預，可能削弱長存續期間美元資產的吸引力。周一沒有化解這項制度性張力，卻證明油價上漲、地緣政治風險回歸時，即使前端政策溢價已到位、通膨補償未變，長端仍可能遭到拋售。

## 緊縮壓力擴及Fed以外

印度交出觀察期間最強的實際成長驚喜。4月至6月一季國內生產毛額年增7.8%，高於7.3%的預估中位數與印度儲備銀行7%的預測。前一季增幅由7.8%上修至8.6%，創現行資料序列新高。成長廣度與整體數字同樣重要：製造業增幅由8.3%加速至9.2%，金融服務由8.8%升至12.1%，固定資本形成總額由5.8%升至11.9%，民間消費則由6.8%升至7.1%。數據公布後，市場提高對稍後升息的權重，10年期公債殖利率上升4個基點至6.95%。

這份成長數據擴大印度儲備銀行因應通膨的空間，卻沒有確定升息時點。央行8月將基準利率維持在5.25%；一名民營部門經濟學家認為，經濟活動強勁且物價偏高，可支持本財政年度下半年緊縮50個基點。首席經濟顧問V. Anantha Nageswaran則指出限制條件：通膨仍在2%-6%的容忍區間內，政策制定者也正觀察第二輪效應。印度近90%的原油仰賴進口，因此荷姆茲海峽風險再起，即使內需強勁，仍可能推高物價、壓縮消費與企業利潤率。債市面對更棘手的取捨：成長讓印度儲備銀行有能力緊縮，新增通膨卻仍有一部分來自外部。

德國8月通膨數據增加歐洲央行升息的依據，幅度卻低於市場所憂慮。消費者物價年增2.9%，高於前值2.8%，為4月以來最高，但低於3.1%的預估中位數。能源推動通膨加速，服務與食品通膨則放緩。數據證實區域能源衝擊正傳導至歐元區最大經濟體，但尚未出現足以迫使央行連續多次升息的廣泛第二輪壓力。存款利率目前為2.25%，眼前爭論是9月如預期升息後，政策是否必須小幅進入限制性區域；最新德國數據本身，尚不足以證明國內經濟持續過熱。

日本的政策訊號更直接。根據一名美國官員對會議內容的說法，Bessent告訴財務大臣片山皋月與日本央行總裁植田和男，日本下一步應該升息。這項表態超越他先前對日本當局將採取適當行動的預期，並把日圓穩定與更明確的正常化路徑連結起來。日圓收在約159.69兌1美元，單日僅升值0.3%，7月干預帶來的升幅則已有一半以上回吐。市場反應說明，美國殖利率維持高檔、日本實質利率仍深度為負時，再一次外匯操作也無法無限期取代政策利率調整。

日本國內存續期間資產變得更具投資吸引力，政策正常化卻也同步提高按市價評價風險。10年期日本公債殖利率一度觸及2.95%，創1996年以來新高，逼近3%門檻。分析師開始主張，政府年金投資基金最終可能把國內債券配置目標由25%提高至30%-35%。以¥318兆資產規模計算，配置每調整1個百分點就超過¥3兆；一項估算顯示，國內債券配置提高至30%與35%，對應的日圓買盤分別接近¥16兆與¥32兆。GPIF在4月至6月已買進¥5.7兆日本債券，至少是2020財政年度以來單季最多。

這些數字代表潛在需求，不是既定決策。GPIF表示，目前環境與其5年期投資組合所依據的假設並無重大差異；批評者則指出，增加債券配置後，基金可能必須在其他部位承擔更多風險，才能維持報酬目標。現有目標是長期報酬率高於名目薪資成長率1.9個百分點。因此，眼前變化雖有條件，影響仍不容忽視：殖利率接近3%，正吸引先前在升息期間反覆承受損失的國內資產負債表；在策略配置真正改變前，若日本央行加快正常化且標售需求疲弱，殖利率仍可能進一步走高。

紐西蘭則以即將到來的政策事件，而非已公布的結果，補足全球圖像。受訪的21名經濟學家全數預期，紐西蘭準備銀行將官方現金利率上調25個基點至2.75%，連續第二次升息；此前第二季通膨升至4.1%，高於1%-3%的目標區間。國內經濟上季可能萎縮，失業率也升至5.6%，創11年新高，但政策制定者希望在預期復甦前，避免燃料與其他供給成本固化。印度、德國、日本與紐西蘭並未處於同一輪同步緊縮循環；各國卻因需求具韌性、匯率承壓或進口能源成本升高而更難按兵不動，共同推高投資人持有存續期間所要求的報酬門檻。

## 本地殖利率重塑資金配置

哥倫比亞承受最明確的主權融資衝擊。即將上任的政府告知造市商，計畫在2026年額外籌措約$110億，並進行債務交換。其中超過$30億預計來自外部借款，以發債為主；另有約25兆披索將由本地市場籌措。先前披露的2027年初步赤字相當於GDP的9.4%，上周五已使10年期本地債殖利率上升超過30個基點，披索一度貶值2.1%；額外融資計畫隨後出爐。周一本地殖利率與交換利率延續升勢，披索再跌0.9%，在新興市場貨幣中表現最差。

市場反應反映供給去化風險，不是單純失去市場准入。哥倫比亞本地債今年仍上漲29%，在新興市場同類債券中報酬最佳；新政府面對的市場，先前一直肯定其高持有收益與政治轉型。新增供給規模足以打破這項平衡。BTG Pactual預期殖利率曲線中段與長端將承受最大調整，後續標售必須揭示，投資人究竟會要求更大讓利，還是降低對較長天期債券的需求。財政部長Miguel Gómez計畫在9月7日當周訪問紐約與華盛頓，並否認哥倫比亞正在尋求國際貨幣基金紓困。多邊融資與可信的財政整頓法案可限制發債規模；兩者若都缺席，公開承接而來的赤字不會立即安撫市場，只會轉化為更高的短期市場出清殖利率。

沙烏地阿拉伯趁市場准入尚未受限，提前分散融資來源。政府正初步洽談至少$80億貸款，Saudi Aramco也另與銀行協商。兩筆交易都尚未定案。關鍵在於，伊朗衝突擾亂貿易、提高進口成本並加劇區域供應鏈壓力之際，沙烏地阿拉伯選擇拓展資金來源。聯貸可以降低對單一債券發行窗口的依賴，卻仍會占用同一批銀行的資產負債表；這些銀行已在為亞洲與波斯灣地區的大型基礎建設及科技計畫提供融資。

巴西顯示，即使沒有新的主權交易，本地高利率仍足以改變投資產業的資金流向。Arminio Fraga認為，兩位數固定收益報酬使獨立避險基金難以留住資產，因此同意把Gavea Investimentos旗下基金移轉至Banco Bradesco。7家大型獨立機構的境內宏觀策略資產自2022年以來減少近半，降至約890億里爾；整體避險基金業同期則錄得6,720億里爾資金流出。大型金融機構旗下宏觀基金逆勢成長，自2019年以來幾乎倍增至5,420億里爾。交易員預期政策利率至少到2027年底仍將高於13%；政府債與享有稅務優惠的公司債，不只改變誰掌握本地儲蓄，也重塑這些資金的配置去向。

智利提供規模較小的反例：樂觀情緒正推動投資人下探較低信用評級。24名分析師與交易員的調查中，17%願意在9月持有評級低至BBB的公司債，比例超過前月3倍，並創3月以來新高；另有26%願意下探至A，26%偏好AA以上，30%則只持有最高評級。這項轉變源自一項削減企業稅與行政障礙的法案取得進展，預定9月上半月立法。自3月以來，價值近$180億的計畫已取得環境許可，預算辦公室預測明年經濟成長3.7%。

信用風險下探仍有主權界線。智利經濟在第一季萎縮0.3%後，第二季陷入停滯；改革預計將使政府收入至少減少5年。債務總額正逼近GDP的45%，部分分析師認為這個區域伴隨降評風險。投資人接受較低評級公司債，是因預期改革將重振成長；但若經濟活動未能迅速回應，同一項改革也可能削弱主權資產負債表。哥倫比亞、巴西與智利因而呈現本地高殖利率的3種不同結果：新增供給突然必須讓利、資金轉向單純的固定收益報酬，以及選擇性下探較低評級公司債。

## 損失分配走向契約化

加州立法者刪除原本最能把野火責任移出企業資產負債表的條款後，公用事業信用債重新定價。PG&E 2056年到期、票息6.3%的債券利差擴大15個基點至138個基點；Edison International 2047年到期、票息4%的債券利差擴大10個基點至133個基點。州長Gavin Newsom原提議禁止保險公司透過代位求償向公用事業追償。周六提出的法案並未納入這項保障，上市公用事業仍須承擔未來索賠，市場因而擔心後續可能遭到降評。

法案仍會改變理賠程序，包括禁止保險公司把對公用事業的求償權出售給投資人、限制須為災難性火災負責的公用事業執行長獎金、加快向受災者付款，以及強化預防措施。這些規定可以改變行政流程與誘因，卻沒有設下資產負債表曝險上限，而債券持有人原本期待更廣泛的提案能降低這類曝險。因此，利差變動源自一項具體法律保障遭到刪除，不只是周一美國公債普遍遭到拋售。預計周二舉行的表決，將決定這套架構是否成為法律。

CDK Global與債權人指導委員會達成協議，讓困境企業再融資進入明確的順位與回收安排。Brookfield Business Partners將把約$6.75億持債交換為順位較低、採實物付息的債券，使贊助方債權居次，同時保留CDK現金。指導委員會貸款人則將2029年到期的有擔保債務，以8%折價交換為到期日延後2.5年的債務。該公司近$40億、2029年到期的定期貸款，上周五成交價約為面額的52美分，反映2024年網路攻擊後，獲利、槓桿與再融資問題有多嚴重。

這筆交易的不尋常之處，在於Brookfield若於交割前繼續在次級市場買債，參與協商的債權人可能面臨更大折價。回購上限接近$12億，折價最高可升至13%。其餘貸款人仍可參與協商，但條件不得優於指導委員會。合作協議也禁止參與的持有人退出，另行達成交易。Moody's 8月初把評級連降2級至Caa2，已反映違約風險；目前協議進一步界定，贊助方債權居次、延長到期日與折價交換將如何在債權人之間分配風險。

UBS在瑞士資本規範辯論中取得明顯較寬鬆的階段性結果。上議院經濟委員會以10票對2票、1票棄權通過建議，主張重新設計的額外第一類資本債，可支應該銀行海外子公司相關約$200億額外資本要求中的最多50%，其餘仍由股權支應。這項決定影響重大：UBS約占2,860億歐元歐洲AT1市場的7%，其未來發行與契約設計的意義遠超過單一銀行。

這項讓步的前提，是讓AT1更早吸收損失。依委員會支持的架構，一旦普通股最低要求遭到突破，股息、庫藏股買回與AT1票息都將停止，獎金池也會縮減。這些觸發條款旨在讓AT1於進入處置程序前就發揮作用，而非等到倒閉時才吸收損失。債務成本通常低於普通股，因此這項建議可降低UBS可能承擔的成本，同時維持政府的要求：海外業務必須由可吸收損失的資本全額支應。

立法風險仍然顯著。上議院預定在9月14日至10月2日會期表決，立場較左傾的下議院可能推翻讓步。財政部質疑AT1能否在危機中可靠吸收損失，社會民主黨也批評委員會立場。因此，目前發展既不是UBS最終獲得寬減，也不是歐洲銀行資本規範的既定範本。這只是政治層面以10票對2票支持一項具體折衷方案：只要觸發機制足具公信力，就可把大型資本要求的一半由普通股轉為或有債務。

上述個別發行人的債權重新定價，廣泛高收益債總報酬卻幾乎未動，兩者並不矛盾。PG&E與Edison面對的是未來侵權責任如何分配的法定決策；CDK債權人協商的是順位、到期日與折價；UBS爭取的則是哪一類證券可以滿足監管資本要求。基準利率會影響各項估值，但目前真正決定價格的資訊，是誰承擔損失，以及相關債權何時可以執行。

## AI融資觸及銀行極限

亞洲資料中心借款規模已大到足以限制早期支應其擴張的銀行市場。2025年初以來，區域貸款規模已近$290億；2026年至今更創$150億紀錄，較去年同期高27%。DayOne Data Centers正洽談把現有融資額度提高至最多$70億，若完成，將成為區域規模最大的資料中心債務融資。銀行業者表示，貸款機構正逼近產業曝險上限，對既有贊助方、報酬與風險移轉安排也變得更挑剔。

銀行已開始管理資產負債表。法國農業信貸銀行尋求出售一筆香港資料中心貸款的部分部位，Morgan Stanley則評估以重大風險移轉交易對沖曝險。這些動作不代表融資窗口已關閉，而是承作銀行在核貸下一個專案前，愈來愈需要先回收資本。資產擔保證券與專案債券可能因此扮演更大角色。美國光纖與資料中心業者去年出售約$230億資產擔保債務，年增86%，為銀行把成熟曝險移出帳簿、轉入長期資本市場提供範本。

Nvidia透過可轉換債券向MediaTek投資$35億，為這波轉移增添另一種工具。這是Nvidia在美國以外規模最大的直接投資，融資同時連結一項把加速運算導入客製化系統的合作關係。可轉換架構為MediaTek提供長期資本，也讓Nvidia分享股權價值，使AI融資循環跨出傳統銀行貸款與無擔保科技債。對債權人而言，這筆交易也說明，銀行業的集中曝險開始形成限制時，策略投資人仍可在資本結構的不同順位供應資金。

專案能否落地，正與融資能力一樣成為信用變數。美國科技公司今年規劃投入超過$7,000億建設AI基礎設施，但2026年前3個月，至少75個、總值約$1,300億的資料中心專案，因地方反對而遭阻擋或延遲。8月調查顯示，61%的美國成年人反對在居住地區新建資料中心，較2月與3月調查高12個百分點。紐約州已暫停超大規模設施，德州則實質凍結新開發案。只有許可、電力與社區接受度都能讓標的資產開始營運時，由設備、租約或未來產能擔保的債務，才有能力承接建設與再融資風險。

影響不只限於科技信用債。銀行若為一筆可能達$70億的融資額度預留承作空間，就會壓縮其他槓桿型與基礎建設借款人的額度。把貸款轉入ABS或專案債券，也會為已在承接主權發債與活絡公司債供給的機構市場增加供給。可轉換債可以降低現金票息，卻使債權價值與股權表現更緊密連動。融資體系正透過分銷與工具選擇調整，但每一項調整都只是移轉風險，沒有消除風險。

## 前瞻市場意義

美國數據隨即開始檢驗周一的實質殖利率賣壓。8月S&P製造業PMI終值定於9月1日紐約時間上午9時45分公布，上午10時接著公布ISM製造業指數、7月職缺與營建支出。若ISM接近55.2的市場共識，尤其訂單、就業與價格分項強勁，且職缺接近730萬個預估，將支持美國經濟足以承受Jackson Hole會議後市場所反映利率路徑的看法。若就業廣度疲弱或訂單明顯流失，2年期殖利率持平將比周一長端利率上升更具資訊性。周五非農就業報告與9月11日通膨數據，接著將決定10年期殖利率收在4.75%，會成為持久的實質利率水準，還是隨市場移除緊縮溢價而回落。

日本10年期公債周二東京時間下午12時35分標售，是殖利率接近3%時首次直接的去化考驗。上次標售投標倍數為2.56倍，是2025年5月以來最弱；2年期標售需求不佳，也已顯示市場在9月17日至18日日本央行會議前態度謹慎。需求強勁代表，即使GPIF尚未調整任何策略目標，國內投資人已開始認為目前殖利率足以補償風險。若結果再度疲弱，市場將要求更大讓利，日本存續期間壓力外溢至其他主權殖利率曲線的風險也會升高。紐西蘭周三預計將利率升至2.75%，則會另行顯示另一家央行是否願意在經濟活動疲弱時仍升息，以遏止輸入型通膨。

法律與融資能否順利執行，將決定目前分歧繼續停留在個別發行人，還是擴大至更廣市場。加州周二表決將決定，公用事業是否維持先前導致PG&E與Edison利差擴大的野火責任架構。哥倫比亞接下來的標售與財政部長9月會議，將顯示要在本地市場籌措25兆披索、由外部籌措超過$30億，必須提供多少讓利。DayOne潛在$70億貸款的最終條款，則會顯示銀行能否在不削弱保障或定價的情況下，再聯貸一筆創紀錄的資料中心融資。執行順利可維持市場准入，並把風險配置給已獲明確補償的持有人；表決失敗、標售疲弱或銀行被迫分銷帳上部位，則表示基準殖利率上升正開始放大個別發行人的限制。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Renewed fighting around the Strait of Hormuz turned Friday's policy repricing into a broader test of duration, but the closing structure stopped short of confirming a new inflation shock. The 10-year Treasury yield rose 2 basis points to 4.75%, its highest level since January 2025, and the 30-year added 3 basis points to 5.25%. The 2-year held at 4.34%, leaving the adjustment concentrated beyond the front end and steepening 2s10s by 2 basis points to 41 basis points and 2s30s by 3 basis points to 91 basis points. WTI futures climbed 3.55% to $86.36 after the United States and Iran exchanged attacks for the first time in about a month. The combination kept the Federal Reserve's inflation response in focus while returning energy, term premium and supply absorption to the long-end discussion.

The details argue for a measured interpretation of that selloff. The 10-year real yield increased 2 basis points to 2.44%, matching the rise in the nominal yield, while the 10-year breakeven was unchanged at 2.31%. Brent futures also moved against the simple energy-inflation narrative, falling 0.81% to $88.59 even as WTI surged. Investors demanded more real compensation and pushed the curve steeper; they did not mark up 10-year inflation compensation on the day. The 10-year yield was unchanged over the full month and the 30-year remained 2 basis points lower, so Monday's move extended the immediate pressure without erasing the longer-horizon support from Treasury's planned buybacks or establishing that the fiscal term premium had broken higher again.

Cross-asset trading located the stress in duration and rate-sensitive growth rather than in a generalized financing retreat. The S&P 500 fell 0.58%, the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.62% and the semiconductor index declined 2.92%, while the Dollar Index gained 0.26%. Investment-grade credit's total-return gauge fell 0.49%, consistent with its longer duration, but the principal high-yield gauges slipped only about 0.07%. Gold rose 0.44% and remained up 11.09% for the month. That mix leaves two forces in tension: a firmer real discount rate is weighing on long-duration assets, while demand for protection against policy, currency and geopolitical uncertainty has not disappeared.

The session therefore changed the shape of the risk, not the underlying requirement for policy follow-through. Friday's hawkish message had raised the policy-sensitive part of the curve; Monday's oil move left the 2-year unchanged and pushed the long end higher. The weekly record still shows the earlier bear flattening, with the 2-year up 10 basis points against gains of 5 basis points at 10 years and 2 basis points at 30 years. The daily steepening says that credible Fed restraint alone cannot insulate long bonds from an energy interruption, heavy September corporate supply or uncertainty over Treasury intervention. Yet flat breakevens say those risks have not become a self-reinforcing inflation judgment. The next data must distinguish whether a 4.75% 10-year yield reflects durable real-rate pressure or a temporary premium for an eventful week.

## Oil Reopens the Long-End Question

The underlying geopolitical event was sufficiently concrete to affect the completed close. American forces struck an island in the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran retaliated with attacks directed at the United Arab Emirates and Jordan. President Donald Trump then threatened additional action during the U.S. session. WTI reached a level above $86 as the market reconsidered hopes that traffic through Hormuz was normalizing. This was not merely another diplomatic warning: the first direct exchange in about a month restored the possibility that physical disruption and higher transport costs could persist into the autumn inflation data.

The Treasury response nevertheless separated immediate commodity risk from medium-term inflation expectations. Five-year yields rose 1 basis point to 4.49%, the 10-year reached 4.75%, and the 30-year moved to 5.25%, while the 2-year stayed at the level established after the Fed chair's speech. A pure escalation in expectations for the September policy rate would normally place more pressure near the front end. Instead, Monday added compensation farther out, where energy persistence, future issuance and uncertainty over the interaction between fiscal and monetary policy carry greater weight. The real-yield increase reinforces that reading. Investors raised the required inflation-adjusted return even though 10-year breakevens did not move.

Month-end demand offered little visible counterweight. Nearly 244,000 December 10-year note futures traded within one minute around the 4 p.m. New York index rebalancing, close to 10% of the day's volume, yet long Treasuries derived scant closing benefit. Options demand also shifted toward protection against a deeper long-bond decline, including roughly $6.5 million spent on December Treasury-bond puts associated with a 30-year yield near 5.7% by their November 20 expiry. Those trades are hedges rather than forecasts, but their location shows where investors saw the most asymmetric risk after the front end had already repriced.

Treasury's expanded buyback plan still constrained the comparison across sovereign markets. Secretary Scott Bessent noted that the U.S. 10-year yield had risen only about 2 basis points in August, against increases exceeding 10 basis points in Germany and 15 basis points in Japan. His defense of the program was new in tone: he said the aim was to slow one-way market behavior and argued that Treasuries might have performed worse without the intervention. He also moved the timing of a promised fiscal-consolidation presentation from the near term to the coming weeks or months. The first point supports long-end liquidity; the second leaves the fiscal anchor less immediate. Neither changes the amount the government must finance.

The dollar added only 0.26% on Monday and remained 0.38% lower over the month, despite the rise in real yields. That restraint matters because an unambiguous policy divergence in favor of the United States would normally provide stronger currency support. Investors continue to weigh Fed credibility against concern that larger buybacks and a more interventionist Treasury weaken the appeal of long-duration dollar assets. Monday did not resolve that institutional tension. It showed that when oil rises and geopolitical risk returns, the long end can sell off even with the front-end policy premium already in place and inflation compensation unchanged.

## Tightening Broadens Beyond the Fed

India supplied the strongest realized growth surprise in the window. Gross domestic product expanded 7.8% from a year earlier in the April-June quarter, above the 7.3% median estimate and the Reserve Bank of India's 7% forecast. The previous quarter was revised to 8.6% from 7.8%, the highest rate in the current data series. The breadth was as important as the headline: manufacturing growth accelerated to 9.2% from 8.3%, financial services to 12.1% from 8.8%, gross fixed capital formation to 11.9% from 5.8%, and private consumption to 7.1% from 6.8%. The 10-year government-bond yield rose 4 basis points to 6.95% after the release as the market assigned more weight to a later rate increase.

That growth result changes the RBI's room to respond to inflation rather than settling the timing. The central bank held its benchmark at 5.25% in August, and one private-sector economist argued that robust activity and elevated prices could justify 50 basis points of tightening in the second half of the fiscal year. Chief Economic Adviser V. Anantha Nageswaran offered the limiting view that inflation remained within the 2%-6% tolerance band and that policymakers were watching for second-round effects. India also imports nearly 90% of its crude, so the renewed Hormuz risk can raise prices, squeeze consumption and compress corporate margins even when domestic demand is strong. The bond-market consequence is a less comfortable trade-off: growth gives the RBI capacity to tighten, while the source of incremental inflation remains partly external.

Germany's August inflation release added evidence for an ECB increase, although it was milder than feared. Consumer prices rose 2.9% from a year earlier, up from 2.8% and the strongest reading since April, but below the 3.1% median estimate. Energy drove the acceleration; services and food inflation eased. The report confirms that the regional energy shock is reaching the largest euro-area economy without yet showing the broader second-round pressure that would compel a long sequence of increases. At a 2.25% deposit rate, the immediate debate is whether policy must move mildly into restrictive territory after the expected September step, not whether the latest German print alone proves persistent domestic overheating.

Japan's policy signal became more direct. Bessent told Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama and Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda that Japan's next step should be to raise rates, according to an account of their meeting from a U.S. official. The statement went beyond his earlier expectation that Japanese authorities would act appropriately and tied yen stabilization to a clearer normalization path. The yen finished near 159.69 per dollar, only 0.3% stronger on the day and still having surrendered more than half of the gain produced by the July intervention. That response shows why another foreign-exchange operation cannot substitute indefinitely for a policy-rate adjustment when U.S. yields remain high and Japanese real rates remain deeply negative.

Domestic duration is becoming more investable at the same time that normalization raises mark-to-market risk. Japan's 10-year government-bond yield touched 2.95%, its highest since 1996 and close to the 3% threshold. Analysts have begun to argue that the Government Pension Investment Fund could eventually lift its domestic-bond target from 25% to 30%-35%. On a ¥318 trillion asset base, a 1-percentage-point allocation shift represents more than ¥3 trillion; one estimate put the yen purchases associated with a 30% domestic-bond allocation near ¥16 trillion and a 35% allocation near ¥32 trillion. GPIF already bought ¥5.7 trillion of Japanese debt in April-June, the most in a quarter since at least fiscal 2020.

Those figures describe potential demand, not a decision. GPIF said the current environment was not materially different from the assumptions behind its five-year portfolio, and critics noted that increasing bonds could require more risk elsewhere to preserve the fund's return objective. The existing target seeks a long-run return 1.9 percentage points above nominal wage growth. The current shift is therefore conditional but consequential: yields near 3% are attracting domestic balance sheets that absorbed repeated losses as rates rose, while a faster BOJ path and weak auction demand can still push those yields higher before strategic allocations change.

New Zealand completes the global picture as a scheduled rather than realized policy event. All 21 surveyed economists expect the Reserve Bank of New Zealand to raise the official cash rate 25 basis points to 2.75%, its second consecutive increase, after inflation reached 4.1% in Q2 and moved above the 1%-3% target range. The domestic economy may have contracted last quarter and unemployment reached an 11-year high of 5.6%, but policymakers are trying to prevent fuel and other supply costs from becoming embedded before a projected recovery. India, Germany, Japan and New Zealand are not following one synchronized cycle. They are converging on a higher hurdle for duration because resilient demand, currency pressure or imported energy costs have made inaction more difficult.

## Local Yield Reshapes Capital Pools

Colombia delivered the clearest sovereign funding shock. The incoming administration told market makers that it planned to raise about $11 billion of additional financing in 2026 and conduct debt swaps. More than $3 billion is expected to come from external borrowing, mainly bond sales, and about 25 trillion pesos from the local market. That incremental plan arrived after disclosure of a preliminary 2027 deficit equal to 9.4% of GDP had already pushed 10-year local yields more than 30 basis points higher and weakened the peso as much as 2.1% on Friday. On Monday, local yields and swap rates extended their increase and the peso fell another 0.9%, the worst performance among emerging-market currencies.

The market reaction reflects absorption risk rather than a simple loss of access. Colombia's local bonds remain up 29% this year, the strongest return among their emerging-market peers, so the new government is approaching a market that has rewarded its high carry and political transition. The added supply is large enough to change that balance. BTG Pactual expects the belly and long end to bear the greatest adjustment, and the next auctions must reveal whether investors require larger concessions or reduce demand for longer maturities. Finance Minister Miguel Gómez plans to visit New York and Washington in the week of September 7, while rejecting the idea that Colombia is seeking an IMF rescue. Multilateral funding and a credible fiscal-consolidation law could limit bond issuance; without them, transparency about the inherited deficit becomes a higher near-term clearing yield rather than immediate reassurance.

Saudi Arabia is pursuing diversification before access becomes constrained. The sovereign is in early discussions for a loan of at least $8 billion, and Saudi Aramco is holding separate talks with banks. Neither transaction is final. Their significance lies in the decision to broaden funding while the Iran conflict disrupts trade, raises import costs and strains regional supply chains. A syndicated loan can reduce reliance on one bond-market window, but it draws on the same bank balance sheets that are already financing large infrastructure and technology programs across Asia and the Gulf.

Brazil shows how high local rates can redirect an investor industry even without a new sovereign transaction. Arminio Fraga agreed to transfer Gavea Investimentos' funds to Banco Bradesco after concluding that double-digit fixed-income returns made it difficult for an independent hedge fund to retain assets. Seven large independent firms' onshore macro assets have fallen nearly by half since 2022 to about 89 billion reais, and the broader hedge-fund industry has recorded 672 billion reais of withdrawals over the same period. Macro funds inside large financial institutions have moved in the opposite direction, nearly doubling since 2019 to 542 billion reais. With traders expecting the policy rate to remain above 13% through at least the end of 2027, government and tax-advantaged corporate debt are changing who controls local savings as well as what those savings own.

Chile offers a smaller counterexample in which optimism is pushing investors down the quality spectrum. In a survey of 24 analysts and traders, 17% were willing to own corporate bonds rated as low as BBB for September, more than triple the previous month's share and the highest since March. Another 26% would go as low as A, 26% preferred AA or above, and 30% stayed with the highest ratings. The shift followed progress on a bill cutting corporate taxes and administrative barriers, scheduled to become law in the first half of September. Projects worth almost $18 billion have received environmental approval since March, and the budget office forecasts 3.7% growth next year.

That risk extension still has a sovereign boundary. Chile's economy stagnated in Q2 after contracting 0.3% in Q1, and the reform is expected to reduce government revenue for at least five years. Gross debt is moving toward the 45%-of-GDP area that some analysts associate with downgrade risk. Investors are accepting lower corporate ratings because they expect reform to revive growth, yet the same reform can weaken the sovereign balance sheet if activity does not respond quickly enough. Colombia, Brazil and Chile therefore illustrate three distinct consequences of high local yield: a sudden supply concession, migration toward simple fixed-income returns, and selective movement into lower-rated corporate debt.

## Loss Allocation Gets Contractual

California utility credit repriced after lawmakers removed the provision that had offered the clearest transfer of wildfire liability away from company balance sheets. The spread on PG&E's 6.3% bond due in 2056 widened 15 basis points to 138 basis points, while Edison International's 4% notes due in 2047 widened 10 basis points to 133 basis points. Governor Gavin Newsom had proposed preventing insurers from pursuing utilities through subrogation. The bill introduced Saturday did not adopt that protection, leaving publicly traded utilities exposed to future claims and prompting concern that rating downgrades could follow.

The legislation still changes the claims process. It would prohibit insurers from selling claims against utilities to investors, restrict bonuses for chief executives of utilities liable for catastrophic fires, accelerate payments to survivors and increase prevention efforts. Those measures can affect administration and incentives, but they do not cap the balance-sheet exposure that bondholders had expected the broader proposal to reduce. The spread move is consequently tied to a specific legal omission rather than to Monday's general Treasury selloff alone. A vote expected Tuesday determines whether that structure becomes law.

CDK Global's agreement with a creditor steering committee moves a distressed refinancing into explicit priority and recovery terms. Brookfield Business Partners would exchange about $675 million of its holdings for lower-ranking paper with payment-in-kind interest, subordinating the sponsor's claim and preserving CDK's cash. Steering-committee lenders would exchange secured obligations due in 2029 for debt maturing 2.5 years later at an 8% discount. The company's nearly $4 billion term loan due in 2029 traded near 52 cents on Friday, reflecting the depth of the earnings, leverage and refinancing problem after the 2024 cyberattack.

The unusual feature is a mechanism that can deepen the negotiating creditors' haircut if Brookfield continues buying debt in the secondary market before closing. Repurchases are capped near $1.2 billion, and the discount can rise as high as 13%. Remaining lenders may now negotiate, but their treatment cannot be better than the steering committee's. A cooperation agreement also prevents participating holders from breaking away for a separate deal. Moody's two-notch downgrade to Caa2 in early August captured the default risk; the current agreement defines how sponsor subordination, maturity extension and discounted exchange could allocate that risk among creditors.

UBS achieved a materially softer interim outcome in Switzerland's capital debate. The upper-house economic committee voted 10-2, with one abstention, to recommend that redesigned Additional Tier 1 debt cover as much as 50% of the roughly $20 billion extra capital requirement associated with the bank's foreign subsidiaries. Equity would still back the remaining portion. The decision is important because UBS accounts for about 7% of the EUR286 billion European AT1 market, making its future issuance and contractual design relevant well beyond one bank.

The concession depends on making the instruments absorb loss earlier. Under the committee-backed framework, a breach of the minimum common-equity requirement would stop dividends, share repurchases and AT1 coupons and reduce the bonus pool. Those triggers are intended to make AT1 function before resolution rather than only at the point of failure. Debt is generally cheaper than common equity, so the recommendation reduces the likely cost to UBS while preserving the government's demand that foreign operations be fully backed by loss-absorbing capital.

Legislative risk remains substantial. The upper house is scheduled to vote during its September 14-October 2 session, and the more left-leaning lower house can reverse concessions. The Finance Ministry has questioned whether AT1 is reliable enough to absorb losses in a crisis, and the Social Democrats criticized the committee's position. The current event is therefore neither final relief for UBS nor a settled template for European bank capital. It is a 10-2 political endorsement of a specific compromise that shifts half of a large requirement from common equity into contingent debt, provided the triggers become credible.

Broad high-yield total returns barely moved even as these issuer-specific claims repriced. That divergence is coherent. PG&E and Edison face a statutory decision about future tort liabilities; CDK creditors are negotiating ranking, maturity and haircut; UBS is contesting which security can satisfy a regulatory capital burden. Benchmark rates affect each valuation, but the decisive current information lies in who bears loss and when that claim becomes enforceable.

## AI Funding Reaches Bank Limits

Asia's data-center borrowing has become large enough to constrain the bank market that financed its early expansion. Loans in the region have reached nearly $29 billion since the start of 2025 and a record $15 billion so far in 2026, 27% above the comparable period last year. DayOne Data Centers is discussing an increase in an existing facility to as much as $7 billion, which would make it the region's largest data-center debt financing. Bankers report that lenders are approaching sector limits and becoming more selective about familiar sponsors, returns and risk transfer.

Balance-sheet management is already visible. Credit Agricole sought to sell part of a Hong Kong data-center loan, while Morgan Stanley explored a significant-risk-transfer transaction to hedge exposure. Those steps do not indicate that financing has closed; they show that originating banks increasingly need to recycle capital before underwriting the next project. The likely destination is a larger role for asset-backed securities and project bonds. U.S. fiber and data-center owners sold about $23 billion of asset-backed debt last year, an 86% increase, providing a model for moving seasoned exposure from bank books into long-term capital markets.

Nvidia's $3.5 billion investment in MediaTek through convertible bonds adds another instrument to that migration. It is Nvidia's largest direct investment outside the United States and links financing to a partnership intended to bring accelerated computing into customized systems. The convertible structure gives MediaTek term capital while allowing Nvidia to participate in equity value, extending the AI funding cycle beyond conventional bank loans and unsecured technology bonds. For creditors, it also demonstrates that strategic investors can supply capital at a different level of the stack when bank concentration is becoming restrictive.

Project execution is becoming a credit variable alongside financing capacity. U.S. technology companies plan more than $700 billion of AI infrastructure spending this year, yet at least 75 data-center projects worth about $130 billion were blocked or delayed by local opposition during the first 3 months of 2026. An August survey found 61% of U.S. adults opposed a new data center in their area, 12 percentage points more than in surveys conducted during February and March. New York has imposed a moratorium on hyperscale facilities, and Texas has an effective freeze on new development. Debt backed by equipment, leases or future capacity can absorb construction and refinancing risk only if permits, power and community acceptance allow the underlying asset to become operational.

The fixed-income consequence reaches beyond technology credit. Banks that reserve capacity for a potential $7 billion facility have less room for other leveraged and infrastructure borrowers. Moving loans into ABS or project bonds adds supply to institutional markets already absorbing sovereign issuance and an active corporate calendar. Convertibles reduce cash coupons but connect creditor value more closely to equity performance. The funding system is adapting through distribution and instrument choice, yet each adaptation transfers risk rather than eliminating it.

## Forward Market Significance

U.S. data begin testing Monday's real-yield selloff immediately. The final August S&P manufacturing PMI is scheduled for September 1 at 9:45 a.m. New York time, followed at 10:00 a.m. by the ISM manufacturing index, July job openings and construction spending. ISM near its 55.2 consensus, especially with firm orders, employment and prices, together with vacancies near the 7.3 million estimate, would support the view that the economy can tolerate the rate path implied after Jackson Hole. Weak employment breadth or a marked loss of orders would make the unchanged 2-year yield more informative than Monday's rise in long rates. Friday's payroll report and the September 11 inflation release then determine whether the 10-year's 4.75% close becomes a durable real-rate level or retreats as the market removes a tightening premium.

Japan's 10-year auction at 12:35 p.m. Tokyo time on Tuesday is the first direct absorption test at yields near 3%. The previous sale's 2.56 bid-to-cover ratio was the weakest since May 2025, and a poor 2-year auction has already shown caution ahead of the September 17-18 BOJ meeting. Strong demand would indicate that domestic investors are beginning to treat the yield level as adequate compensation even before GPIF changes any strategic target. Another weak result would push the burden toward a larger concession and raise the risk that Japanese duration pressure spills into other sovereign curves. New Zealand's expected increase to 2.75% on Wednesday will separately show whether another central bank is willing to tighten through weak activity to contain imported inflation.

Legal and funding execution can keep current dispersion idiosyncratic or broaden it. California's Tuesday vote determines whether utilities retain the wildfire-liability structure that widened PG&E and Edison spreads. Colombia's coming auctions and the finance minister's September meetings will reveal how much concession is needed to place 25 trillion pesos locally and more than $3 billion externally. Final terms for DayOne's potential $7 billion loan will show whether banks can syndicate another record data-center facility without weakening protection or price. Smooth execution would preserve access while assigning risk to clearly compensated holders; failed votes, weak auctions or forced balance-sheet distribution would show that higher benchmark yields are beginning to amplify issuer-specific constraints.
